newsitem.title: SOUTH AFRICA: De Beers share up on possible Russia deal.
newsitem.headline: De Beers share up on possible Russia deal.

text.p: Shares in diamond mining giant De Beers leapt in early trade on Monday on hopes for a deal with Russia, helped by overall positive sentiment in the wider market, dealers and analysts said.

"Some sort of deal might be on the cards. What is important is what is in the agreement. Does it mean more or less gems for De Beers and are they of quality or not?" said Hennie Vermeulen, mining analyst at Investec Securities.
After touching a high of 148.00 rand the share price settled at 147.50 rand, a rise of 400 cents, or 2.79 percent, in a volume of 187,900 shares valued at over 27 million rand.
De Beers stopped purchases of Russian diamonds at the end of last year when it cancelled its interim arrangement after Russia failed to approve or reject a new trade deal.
On Saturday Russian Finance Minister Alexander Livshits was quoted by Interfax news agency as saying that a compromise had been found "which represents the interests of both Russia and De Beers".
De Beers' Moscow representative Raymond Clark said on Monday that recent talks had been constructive but there was no deal yet.

The share price has risen steadily this year and dealers said there had been continued good demand for De Beers as it was a blue chip. Market sentiment was high on Monday on the back of stronger long bonds, firmer rand and a good January reserves figure released on Friday.
"There has been good demand for De beers from Friday and in New York. Technically it is looking good," a dealer said.
